question: Should OpenClaw add `agents.list[].subagents.workspace` for same-agent default child workspace isolation, or keep explicit `agentId` profiles plus `requireAgentId` as the supported security boundary?
rationale: This changes which workspace files default child subagents can access and adds public config, so automation should not decide the workspace isolation policy.

options.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
options.body: Preserve the current model where safe isolation uses `requireAgentId` and configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

options.title: Add Narrow Opt-In Config
options.body: Implement `subagents.workspace` only as a strict opt-in default-child override with schema, docs, doctor/security review, and targeted tests.

options.title: Defer To Broader Isolation Design
options.body: Handle this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87253 so workspace, cwd, sandbox, and skill workdir isolation are designed as one policy.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Profiles
recommendation.body: Preserve the current model where safe isolation uses `requireAgentId` and configured child agent profiles with their own workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Current checked lines and recent subagent/config area history make this the best available routing candidate for the product/security boundary choice.
